section_summary: This final section concludes a detailed investigative report on Japanese-owned firms, frozen assets, employee networks, deportees, and suspected subversive activity in Peru. It then contains FBI and military-intelligence correspondence and reports concerning Japanese movements between Uruguay and Argentina, the alleged JAPSA espionage network in Colombia, maritime intelligence collection in Argentina, and Japanese publications seized in Brazil. The remaining documents concern information requests about Japanese activities and propaganda throughout Latin America, a Mexican Proclaimed List inquiry, and the wartime “Alert” incident in Costa Rica.

subfiles.title: Investigative report on Japanese firms and nationals in Peru (continued)
subfiles.from: Federal Bureau of Investigation investigative sources
subfiles.to: U.S. government intelligence and diplomatic officials
subfiles.about: Continues an investigation of Japanese-controlled businesses, assets, employees, deportees, and suspected subversive connections in Peru.
subfiles.summary: The report concludes its discussion of Southern Cotton Company assets and then examines Peru Menka, its Sayapullo mining interests, company books, travel payments, and employees who were repatriated or deported. It profiles Sociedad Agrícola Retes and its haciendas, including Hajime Kishi and Nakataro Aray, and records unusual remittances to Japan. It finally describes Nonomiya Shoten's officers, payroll and balance sheet and notes the liquidation or transfer of Japanese firms under Peruvian expropriation law.

subfiles.title: Transmittal on movements of Japanese between Uruguay and Argentina
subfiles.from: J. Edgar Hoover, Director, Federal Bureau of Investigation
subfiles.to: Adolf A. Berle, Department of State
subfiles.about: Transmits an investigative report concerning allegations of extensive Japanese travel between Uruguay and Argentina.
subfiles.summary: Hoover opened inquiries after allegations of Japanese traveling between Uruguay and Argentina, sending the report to officials in Montevideo and Buenos Aires.

subfiles.title: Movements of Japanese between Uruguay and Argentina
subfiles.about: Reports interviews and neighborhood inquiries concerning individual Japanese residents of Uruguay and travel to Argentina.
subfiles.summary: Investigator interviewed Seisho, Delgado and Karaichi and others, mostly flower growers or quiet residents, and found no subversive activity.

subfiles.title: FBI transmittal concerning the JAPSA case
subfiles.from: J. Edgar Hoover, Director, Federal Bureau of Investigation
subfiles.to: Adolf A. Berle, Jr., Assistant Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Transmits additional confidential information on persons connected with the JAPSA case in Colombia.
subfiles.summary: FBI JAPSA memo: most people discussed have left Colombia; Tatekawa and Doku remain under investigation; reliable information distributed to embassies and military and naval intelligence.

subfiles.title: Report on the JAPSA espionage network in Colombia
subfiles.from: Federal Bureau of Investigation confidential sources
subfiles.to: U.S. Department of State and military intelligence agencies
subfiles.about: Examines Japanese trading agencies and individuals in Colombia alleged to have collected intelligence and procured strategic materials for Japan.
subfiles.summary: The report alleges that the JAPSA network operated through the Japanese Embassy in Santiago and commercial organizations such as the Nipon Trade Agency, Japan-Colombia Trading Company and Agencia Comercial Japonesa. It profiles Shinichi Suganami, Katujiro Bando, Keizo Yasuma, Koichi Ogawa, Kosuke Kobayashi, Shigeki Tatekawa and Eduardo Doku, tracing their travel, official connections, scrap-metal purchases and suspected contacts with German interests. Reproduced correspondence confirms that several agents traveled under Japanese government instructions to organize trade bodies, study mining and cotton, and procure scrap iron. The report concludes that only Doku and Tatekawa remained in Colombia.

subfiles.title: Mexico City despatch concerning Mr. Saavedra and a possible Proclaimed List recommendation
subfiles.from: Thomas H. Lockett, Commercial Attaché, for the U.S. Ambassador in Mexico
subfiles.about: Assesses whether the limited information about Mr. Saavedra and his connection to Compañía Petrolera Veracruzana justified Proclaimed List action.
subfiles.summary: The beginning of the despatch is largely illegible and page 521 contains no readable OCR. The surviving conclusion says Saavedra was mentioned only casually and merely appeared to possess authority to sign some company correspondence. Lockett therefore finds insufficient evidence to recommend placing him on the Proclaimed List.

subfiles.title: Memorandum on the Coordinator's request for data on Japanese activities
subfiles.about: Alerts State Department colleagues to an impending request for information about Japanese activities in the other American republics.
subfiles.summary: Duggan says the Coordinator of Inter-American Affairs wants data on Japanese activities in Latin America; given the broad request, he proposes assembling available information before instructing missions.

subfiles.title: Letter forwarding a request on Japanese activities and propaganda
subfiles.from: Edward H. Robbins, Assistant to the Coordinator
subfiles.to: Arthur A. Compton, Department of State
subfiles.about: Forwards a memorandum requesting general information about Japanese activities and propaganda.
subfiles.summary: Robbins asks Compton for State's information on the attached memorandum, and reminds him of a September 22 request on Catholic hierarchies' attitudes.

subfiles.title: Memorandum requesting a study of Japanese activities and propaganda in Latin America
subfiles.about: Requests State Department information for a comprehensive study of Japanese communities, official policy, propaganda and Axis relationships in Latin America.
subfiles.summary: Robbins relays a request for a broad study of Japanese activities and propaganda in Latin America: colonies, politics, Tokyo's policies, German and Italian relations and future problems.

subfiles.title: Intelligence summary on Hara & Cia. and Japanese maritime espionage in Argentina
subfiles.to: State Department, ONI, FBI and Treasury Department
subfiles.about: Identifies a Buenos Aires textile firm as a center for collecting and forwarding maritime intelligence to Japan.
subfiles.summary: Intelligence summary: Noburo Hara and Company received shipping information and contacted Japanese operatives, avoiding blacklisting by nominal ownership transfers; criticizes Argentina's weak controls.

subfiles.title: FBI memorandum on Japanese publications confiscated in Brazil
subfiles.from: John Edgar Hoover, Director, Federal Bureau of Investigation
subfiles.to: Adolf A. Berle, Jr., Assistant Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Notifies the State Department that Portuguese translations of Japanese publications seized in Porto Alegre can be sent to Washington for examination.
subfiles.summary: Hoover reports Porto Alegre police confiscated Japanese publications translated into Portuguese; he asks Berle to identify titles State wants.

subfiles.title: List of Japanese publications confiscated at Porto Alegre
subfiles.about: Lists forty confiscated publications by English and Portuguese title with attributed authors or issuing bodies.
subfiles.summary: List of Japanese publications confiscated at Porto Alegre: dictionaries, agriculture, radio, medicine and education, plus war, economic control, Sino-Japanese War and Nogi and Togo biographies.

subfiles.title: State Department request for selected confiscated Japanese publications
subfiles.from: I. Wilder Spaulding, Chief, Division of Research and Publication
subfiles.to: John Edgar Hoover, Department of Justice
subfiles.about: Requests four titles from the Japanese publications available at Porto Alegre.
subfiles.summary: Spaulding asks Hoover to obtain works on wartime economic laws, the history of war, a Sino-Japanese War album, and rural and youth questions.

subfiles.title: Index-and-return routing slip
subfiles.about: Directs that the preceding correspondence be indexed and returned with any earlier related correspondence.
subfiles.summary: Index-and-return routing slip, half-hour option and request to check marked.

subfiles.title: FBI transmittal concerning the Alert incident
subfiles.from: J. Edgar Hoover, Director, Federal Bureau of Investigation
subfiles.to: Adolf A. Berle, Jr., Assistant Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Transmits additional confidential information about the Alert incident in Costa Rica.
subfiles.summary: Hoover reports further information on the Alert incident from a confidential source, also sent to naval intelligence and General Kroner.

subfiles.title: Report on the Alert incident
subfiles.about: Reconstructs the tuna boat Alert's movement between Puntarenas and Caldera before it was attacked by United States aircraft.
subfiles.summary: Report: the Alert, with a Japanese crew, turned back to Puntarenas with oil aboard; the aerial attack came after return began; Port Captain Beeche reportedly declined an account over his financial interest.
